tip: -하오니 is a formal written 'since': 폐관하오니 (pyegwanhaoni = since it closes).
-하였음을 (-hayeosseumeul) packs a whole clause into one formal noun: 결심하였음을 (gyeolsimhayeosseumeul) = 'that I have decided' – the compressed style of official notices.
-고자 = formal 'in order to': 보답하고자 (bodapagoja = in order to repay).
회신하여 (hoesinhayeo = reply) comes from 회신하다 (hoesinhada), the formal business word for everyday 답장하다 (dapjanghada = to reply).
-(으)로 인하여 = formal 'due to': 악화로 인하여 (akwaro inhayeo = due to worsening).
-(으)ㄹ 따름입니다 = formal 'simply/nothing but': 감사할 따름입니다 (gamsahal ttareumimnida = simply grateful).
-십시오 (-sipsio) is the formal 'please do' of announcements and official documents: 제출해 주십시오 (jechulhae jusipsio) = please submit. Everyday politeness uses -세요 (-seyo).
-에 지나지 않다 = formal 'nothing more than': 것에 지나지 않습니다 (geose jinaji anseumnida = is nothing but).
-시어 is a formal honorific connective 'and/so': 준비하시어 (junbihasieo = please prepare and…).
-여야 하다 is formal written 'must': 판단하여야 합니다 (pandanhayeoya hamnida = must judge).
안내 말씀 드리겠습니다 (annae malsseum deurigetseumnida) is the set formal opener for announcements.
-(이)오나 = formal written 'although': 상황이오나 (sanghwang-iona = though it is the situation).
-(으)ㄹ 시에는 = formal 'in the event that': 위반할 시에는 (wibanhal sieneun = in case of violation).
-(이)라 할지라도 = formal 'even if': 생명이라 할지라도 (saengmyeong-ira haljirado = even if it is a life).
-이야말로 = formal emphatic 'the very': 소통이야말로 (sotong-iyamallo = communication indeed).
-에 한하여 = formal 'limited to': 예약을 하신 분에 한하여 (yeyageul hasin bune hanhayeo = only those who booked).
치하하며 (chihahamyeo = commending) comes from 치하하다 (chihahada), formal vocabulary a superior normally uses to praise effort.
-에 근거하여 = formal 'pursuant to': 법령에 근거하여 (beomnyeonge geun-geohayeo = pursuant to statutes).
머리 숙여 (meori sugyeo = bowing one's head) intensifies a formal apology.
백년가약 (baengnyeon-gayak = lifelong marriage vow) is a formal idiom for wedding congratulations.
-이오니 = formal written 'since it is': 11시이오니 (yeolhan-si-ioni = since it is 11 o'clock).
-는 바입니다 = formal written 'we hereby': 요청하는 바입니다 (yocheonghaneun baimnida = we hereby request).
삼가 주시기 바랍니다 (samga jusigi baramnida) = 'we ask that you refrain' – a set formula on Korean signs. 삼가다 (samgada) asks you to hold back rather than saying 'don't'.
-(으)리라 is a formal literary conjecture/resolve: 되리라 (doerira = it shall become).
말씀을 올리다 (malsseumeul ollida) is literally 'offer words upward' – the humble replacement for 말하다 (malhada = to say) when addressing honored guests.
그림의 떡 (geurime tteok = rice cake in a painting) = something desirable but out of reach.
하늘의 별 따기 (haneure byeol ttagi = picking a star) = nearly impossible to achieve.
티끌 모아 태산 (tikkeul moa taesan = dust piles into a mountain) = small amounts add up big.
우물 안 개구리 (umul an gaeguri = frog in a well) = a person of narrow experience.
제 말 하면 온다 (je mal hamyeon onda = comes when spoken of) = speak of the devil.
